description: We are a team of students from TEC enthusiastic to learn more about how Sphere X contributes to stellar mapping, we want to understand their approach so we can contribute with creative and impactful ideas.
summary: But how can we make this information accessible to people without an astronomy background? How can scientific data become an opportunity to explore, learn, and discover? These questions inspired SPHEREx Data Explorer: A Sky in Motion, a web platform developed by Made On Earth Team to transform SPHEREx mission data into an interactive, educational, and accessible experience.
details:
The platform is designed as a web application to make exploration accessible across devices. User preferences can be stored locally in the browser.

We also distinguish between real scientific information and demonstration resources. Some spectral visualizations, quality indicators, and light curves in demonstration sections use simulated data and are labeled accordingly.

Features that access real SPHEREx observations depend on the availability of external services and the connection to the IRSA archive.

Images and visual resources are obtained from NASA sources, including the NASA Image and Video Library and NASA Science, with appropriate credits provided.

Our Purpose

We believe the universe is full of stories we have yet to discover. Some are hidden in light we cannot see, others in subtle changes that take place over years, and many are waiting for someone curious enough to look closer.

With SPHEREx Data Explorer: A Sky in Motion, we want to bring those stories closer to everyone. We want students to discover something new, people with no astronomy background to explore the sky for the first time, and experienced users to find tools that support further investigation.

Because science often begins with a question, an image that sparks curiosity, or the desire to understand something that once seemed beyond our reach.

The sky is in motion. Our goal is to give everyone the opportunity to discover it.
